problem: The symbol i in i² = 2qIB is never defined, so a student cannot tell whether it is a current, a current density or the RMS noise current. Every other symbol in the chapter is defined.
fix: Add: 'i is the RMS noise current in amperes (so i² is the mean-square noise current in A²)'.

problem: The abbreviation PSD is used from the heading onwards but never expanded, even though AWGN, SNR and dBm are all spelled out.
fix: First use should read: 'White noise is the ideal noise whose power spectral density (PSD) — the noise power per hertz of bandwidth — is the same at every frequency.'

problem: 'σ² is the average noise power (in watts across 1 Ω)' mixes units: σ² is a mean-square voltage in V², which only equals a power in watts when the resistance is 1 Ω.
fix: 'σ² is the mean-square noise voltage in V²; across a 1 Ω resistance it is numerically equal to the average noise power in watts. σ is the RMS noise voltage in volts.'
